name: Virginia

agency.name: State Council of Higher Education for Virginia (SCHEV)

programs.name: Virginia Commonwealth Award
programs.summary: Need-based grant at Virginia public colleges, set by each college from the FAFSA (or VASA). Most colleges' priority date is around March 1.

programs.name: Virginia Tuition Assistance Grant (VTAG)
programs.summary: For Virginia residents at eligible private nonprofit Virginia colleges, full time. Not based on income. Apply on the college's VTAG form.

award.summary: Up to $5,250 a year for in-person undergraduates (draft).

programs.name: G3 (Get Skilled, Get a Job, Give Back)
programs.summary: Tuition, fees and books at Virginia community colleges in high-demand programs, for families at or under 400% of the federal poverty level, after other grants.

award.summary: Tuition, mandatory fees and books left after Pell and other grants.

programs.name: Two-Year College Transfer Grant
programs.summary: For students who finish an associate degree at a Virginia community college with a 3.0 GPA and transfer to a four-year Virginia college.

aid_steps.title: VASA, only if you can't file the FAFSA
aid_steps.summary: Students who can't file the FAFSA but meet Virginia's in-state tuition rules can use the Virginia Alternative State Aid application (VASA) for state aid.
how: If you filed the FAFSA, mark this step Doesn't apply.
Otherwise, complete VASA by each college's priority date.
watch_out: VASA does not give federal aid such as Pell Grants. Only the FAFSA does.

aid_steps.title: Private Virginia college? Fill in its VTAG form
aid_steps.summary: The Virginia Tuition Assistance Grant isn't triggered by the FAFSA. Each private college has its own short VTAG form.
how: Ask the private college's financial aid office for the VTAG form once you choose it.
Turn it in by the college's priority date (late summer for fall).

counselor_notes: Virginia has no statewide merit scholarship. State aid is need-based and set by each college from the FAFSA (Virginia Commonwealth Award; most priority dates around March 1). VGAP is closed to new students starting fall 2027. Private nonprofit colleges add VTAG (up to $5,250, not need-based, on the college's own form). G3 covers community college tuition in high-demand fields for families at or under 400% of the poverty level, and many four-year colleges offer guaranteed admission agreements for Virginia community college graduates.
